cases.question: If other conditions stay the same, what happens when Lumen aperture area decreases?

response.text: When the Lumen aperture area decreases, less light is admitted to the sensor, assuming all other conditions remain constant. This is because the aperture is the opening through which light enters the optics rig, and a smaller aperture allows less light to pass through. As a result, the sensor receives a lower intensity of light, which can affect the brightness of the recorded image. However, the notes do not provide specific details on how the decrease in light affects the exposure time or the signal-to-noise ratio, which are important factors in image capture.
